title: The King and the Foolish Monkey Guard
text:
A king kept a pet monkey that he loved dearly. The monkey had the run of the palace, went everywhere at the king's side, and was trusted completely. Because he was so devoted, the king gave him a special duty: to stand guard over him while he slept.

One hot afternoon the king lay down for a nap, and the monkey took up his post beside the bed, holding a sword to protect his master. Soon a bee, or in some tellings a fly, came buzzing in and settled on the king's chest. The monkey waved it away. It flew off and came back. He chased it again, and again it returned and landed in the same place.

The monkey grew furious. Determined to finish the pest once and for all, he raised the sword and brought it down with all his strength on the insect. The insect flew away unharmed. The blow split the sleeping king's chest, and he died.

The story is told in the Panchatantra to make a single point: a wise enemy is better than a foolish friend.
lesson: Loyalty is not the same as judgment. When you hand someone power over things that matter, make sure they understand the job, not only that they love you.
source: Panchatantra, The King and the Foolish Monkey
